about: Sift's improvement register (docs/AS_BUILT.md §36). IMP-001 to IMP-036 keep AS_BUILT's known issue numbers. Fields: see src/devkb/register.py.

items.title: current_ratio is always blank
items.impact: The screener can't judge liquidity.
items.notes: Add current assets and liabilities to financial_reports if this metric matters.

items.title: Franking defaults to 100% (Australian) or 0% (foreign)
items.impact: Grossed-up yield is wrong for partly franked payers.
items.notes: Correct affected rows by hand; the correction survives re-ingestion. No automated source exists.

items.title: Shares outstanding is derived, not stored
items.impact: A wrong market value from Yahoo skews the Graham Number, P/B, FCF per share and DCF together.
items.notes: Store shares outstanding from an independent source if data quality problems appear.

items.title: Yahoo's field names are unversioned and change without notice
items.impact: Statements can come back blank after a Yahoo change (happened 2026-10-01).
items.notes: Runbook: rb-yahoo-fields.

items.title: Yahoo blocked from the development environment
items.impact: Live ingestion is tested only on the owner's PC.
items.notes: Resolved by running ingestion on the owner's machine.

items.title: No automated test suite
items.impact: Regressions would surface only by inspection.
items.notes: Resolved 2026-10-02; over 680 tests now.

items.title: .env holds the database password in plain text
items.impact: Standard for one PC; not for hosting.
items.notes: Use the host's secret store in Phase 4.

items.title: One DCF model applied to every sector, including banks
items.impact: Banks and REITs had no estimate.
items.notes: Resolved 2026-10-02 with the DDM.

items.title: DCF used only the latest year's free cash flow
items.impact: Estimates swung with one year's figure.
items.notes: Resolved: 3-year average base.

items.title: One bad ticker could abort a batch
items.impact: A whole night's ingestion could be lost.
items.notes: Resolved: per-ticker isolation and pacing.

items.title: No official index constituent list is bundled
items.impact: The screened universe is whatever allords.txt holds.
items.notes: Source the list from the ASX or S&P each quarter.

items.title: Margin of safety could overflow its column
items.impact: A run crashed at 500 companies.
items.notes: Resolved: values beyond 5000% become blank.

items.title: Valuation committed once per run
items.impact: One crash lost every company's valuation that night.
items.notes: Resolved: per-company commits.

items.title: No flag for one-off special dividends
items.impact: Yields looked huge after capital returns.
items.notes: Resolved: payout ratio warning, later abnormal dividends held out.

items.title: Any ratio could overflow its column
items.impact: Single fields lost whole valuation rows.
items.notes: Resolved: every field clamped to its column.

items.title: Pipeline run by hand
items.impact: Data went stale.
items.notes: Resolved: nightly script and Task Scheduler.

items.title: No way to tell newly cheap companies from value traps
items.impact: Static margin of safety hid the difference.
items.notes: Resolved: trends and the trap warning.

items.title: Fundamentals trend compares only two reports
items.impact: A mid-window dip and recovery is missed.
items.notes: A multi-point check would be the proper fix if false flags become a problem.

items.title: CGT records cover share parcels only
items.impact: Dividends, franking credits, carried losses and corporate actions aren't modelled.
items.notes: A dividends_received table is the natural next step for tax time.

items.title: Price markers need 200 stored days
items.impact: Price signal blank until history builds.
items.notes: One-off backfill with a 1-year price fetch.

items.title: Actions are rule-based with fixed thresholds
items.impact: Rules can't know context such as a takeover bid.
items.notes: Each action carries its reason. Not financial advice.

items.title: Code with a new column broke the live database until the schema was applied
items.impact: Every valuation failed.
items.notes: Resolved: schema applied on start and nightly.

items.title: Phone access uses Basic authentication over plain HTTP
items.impact: On an untrusted network the password could be read.
items.notes: Use only on home Wi-Fi; hosting brings HTTPS and proper sign-in.

items.title: Yahoo's dividend feed mixed in one-off distributions
items.impact: Inflated yields and DDM values.
items.notes: Resolved: dividend_history.py.

items.title: No currency conversion between statements and prices
items.impact: USD and NZD reporters were mis-valued.
items.notes: Resolved; revenue trend still includes currency moves.

items.title: The track record can't be backfilled
items.impact: No results until horizons pass.
items.notes: By design.

items.title: Parcels can't move between portfolios
items.impact: A transfer must be entered as a sale and a buy.
items.notes: A transfer feature would record the change of ownership date and value.

items.title: Watchlist triggers are a state, not an alert
items.impact: Nothing is sent; a trigger met and lost between visits isn't seen.
items.notes: Pairs with notifications (IMP-039).

items.title: The benchmark is the plain average of screened companies
items.impact: Small companies count as much as large ones.
items.notes: A market-cap-weighted benchmark could be added alongside.

items.title: What-if scenarios judge today's data only
items.impact: Can't show whether a scenario would have done better historically.
items.notes: Phase 4 of the admin console: backtesting against the track record.

items.title: Prices stored before 2026-10-06 were dividend-adjusted monthly
items.impact: Small steps at ex-dates in older charts.
items.notes: One-off 2-year price refetch cleans it.

items.title: ETF report reader built before seeing the real file
items.impact: Columns might not have mapped.
items.notes: Resolved 2026-10-06 against the real report.

items.title: LIC NTA is monthly
items.impact: Premium or discount uses NTA about a month old.
items.notes: The NTA date is shown beside the figure.

items.title: Yahoo's analyst and holder data is thin for ASX companies
items.impact: Missing ratings; holder lists mainly overseas funds, top 10 only.
items.notes: Shown as context only.

items.title: Nightly runs cut off with no error
items.impact: Nights not updated.
items.notes: Resolved 2026-10-06: task settings and timed steps.

items.title: No exchange rate for the PNG kina
items.impact: BFL, KSL and SST statements failed nightly.
items.notes: Addressed 2026-10-07 by chaining through USD; not yet confirmed against Yahoo.

items.title: Review the articles migrated from the early as-built sections
items.impact: Parts describe the command line as first built; some may be out of date.
items.notes: Their next review is 2026-11-09.

items.title: No continuous integration
items.impact: Tests run only when someone runs them before pushing.
items.notes: A GitHub Actions workflow running the suite on every push (with a PostgreSQL service) would catch misses.

items.title: No notifications (email or phone)
items.impact: Triggers, nightly failures and review reminders show only in Sift.
items.notes: Needs a sending service; fits Phase 4.

items.title: Coattail: director trades and substantial holder notices
items.impact: Coattail shows fund holdings only.
items.notes: Built 2026-10-09 from ASX's market-wide announcement lists, each notice's PDF read nightly; shown on Coattail tabs, company pages and the dashboard.

items.title: Meaning-based search is built but off
items.impact: Search matches words, not meaning.
items.notes: Switch on with SIFT_EMBEDDINGS=local and sentence-transformers.

items.title: Preferences: Language and region, Notifications
items.impact: Date format and time zone are fixed.
items.notes: The owner will supply the reference screenshot.

items.title: Multi-user Phase 3: sign-in
items.impact: Testers can't sign in; accounts are used only through impersonation.
items.notes: Needs a Supabase project (Sydney); share only the URL and anon key.

items.title: Multi-user Phase 4: hosting
items.impact: Sift runs only on the owner's PC.
items.notes: Supabase Postgres and Fly.io, Sydney.

items.title: Multi-user Phase 5: tester readiness
items.impact: Privacy note, terms, not-advice wording, usage limits, error monitoring, feedback link.

items.title: Backups are manual
items.impact: A disk failure could lose portfolios and the track record since the last manual backup.
items.notes: Until hosting, a scheduled weekly pg_dump to another drive or cloud folder.

items.title: app.js is one 4,000-line file
items.impact: Harder to change safely as Sift grows.
items.notes: Split into modules by page when several people work on pages.

items.title: No alerting or monitoring for nightly failures
items.impact: A failed night is noticed only when someone opens Sift.
items.notes: An email at the end of a failed run; error monitoring when hosted.

items.title: Everything depends on one PC
items.impact: If the PC is off, lost or broken, Sift and its nightly run stop.
items.notes: Resolved by hosting (IMP-044); meanwhile keep backups (IMP-046).

items.title: An admin's open impersonation applies in all their browsers
items.impact: A forgotten session shows everywhere until ended or 8 hours pass.
items.notes: Per-browser sessions arrive with sign-in tokens (Phase 3).

items.title: Yahoo Finance data terms for a public service
items.impact: Showing Yahoo's data to other people may not be permitted; a licensed provider may be needed.
items.notes: Settle before Phase 5 (testers outside the household).

items.title: Dependency updates and security patches
items.impact: Pinned packages age; security fixes need a routine.
items.notes: A quarterly check of requirements.txt against new releases, with the test suite.

items.title: Privacy and retention for testers' personal data
items.impact: Portfolios are sensitive; testers need to know what's kept and for how long.
items.notes: Part of Phase 5: privacy note, export and delete my data.

items.title: Live sync to a Neo4j instance
items.impact: The graph is a nightly snapshot loaded by hand.
items.notes: Write the same nodes and relationships with the Neo4j driver when a running graph is wanted.

items.title: Improve the prediction layer
items.impact: Suggested actions are fixed rules; the track record could teach which signals predict returns.
items.notes: Use the scored history (signal_snapshots, signal_outcomes) to test and weight the rules; holder moves and fund flows from the graph as new features. Needs enough track record first.

items.title: Embeddings in pgvector
items.impact: Meaning-based search compares every row in Python.
items.notes: Move embedding to vector(384) with an HNSW index once hosted on Supabase.

items.title: AI connector for testers
items.impact: The MCP server runs locally for one person.
items.notes: A hosted, signed-in version after Phase 3, or an in-app assistant.

items.title: Overseas fund holdings aren't linked
items.impact: ETF holdings of overseas companies don't link to a Sift company.
items.notes: Sift follows ASX companies only; unmatched lines stay in fund_holdings.

items.title: Sign-in and sign-out events
items.impact: Until Phase 3 a session is a spell of use, not a log-on; there are no failed sign-ins or sign-outs to audit.
items.notes: With Supabase Auth: start a session on sign-in, end it on sign-out, log failed attempts, and decide with the privacy note whether to keep an IP address.

items.title: Prove the notice reader on real ASX notices
items.impact: The reader was built on the forms' published layout and test PDFs laid out the same way; ASX's real PDFs vary by company.
items.notes: Run python -m src.coattail.notices --dry-run on the owner's PC, then check the first week's partial and failed notices; add each new layout to tests/unit/test_notice_reader.py.

items.title: Make notices searchable
items.impact: Searching a director's or substantial holder's name finds nothing; notices are reached through Coattail and company pages.
items.notes: Index the last 90 days of notices in a notices area with words, not numbers: "Perpetual became a substantial holder in GOOD".

items.title: Alerts for director buying and new substantial holders
items.impact: The dashboard shows notices on your companies, but nothing tells you when you're away.
items.notes: A watchlist trigger (director bought on market, holder crossed 5%) and, with hosting, an email.

items.title: Prove the share registry reader on ASX
items.impact: The registry is read from ASX's company details, which couldn't be reached from the build environment; companies may show no registry until it's confirmed.
items.notes: Run python -m src.registries --dry-run on the owner's PC; if ASX gives the registry under another field, add it to read_registry() with a test.

items.title: Check the registries' portal links
items.impact: Registries rename their investor portals (Link became MUFG Corporate Markets); a moved link sends people to an error page.
items.notes: Open each link in REGISTRIES (src/registries.py) once a year and after a registry rebrands.

items.title: Prove each broker's export with a real file
items.impact: The importer recognises brokers by their usual column names; a broker's real file may name or lay out a column differently.
items.notes: Start with CommSec, Sharesies and CMC Invest (the owner's brokers): a real export with figures blanked becomes a test in tests/integration/test_broker_import.py.

items.title: Prove ASIC's short position file on the owner's PC
items.impact: The reader was built from ASIC's published column names; the build environment can't reach ASIC, so the real file's encoding or headings may differ.
items.notes: Run python -m src.ingestion.short_positions --dry-run, then --days 365. If it fails, keep the first lines of the file as a test in tests/unit/test_short_positions.py.

items.title: Crash test simulator for portfolios
items.impact: Shows how a portfolio might fare if the market fell sharply (2008, 2020 or a set fall), in plain words, using each holding's beta and volatility.
items.notes: The owner plans a screen for it (Portfolios, Crash test). Beta and volatility are already worked out nightly into price_statistics; consider fat tails and stressed correlations (ADR-017). Roadmap (2026-10-10): built from IMP-071 (historical scenarios), IMP-072 (Expected Shortfall), IMP-073 (fat tails), IMP-074 (crisis correlations); a page under Portfolios, in React and TypeScript (ADR-018).

items.title: Piotroski F-Score: a Financial health card
items.impact: A proven 9-point health check that separates cheap shares that recover from cheap shares that keep falling: Sift's value-trap problem.
items.notes: Done 2026-10-10: Financial health card on the company page (Sift's first React card), nightly in financial_health, screener fields ready for a column. Not yet changing any action: compare with the track record first (a change would need a rules version). References checked: financial-health article.

items.title: Altman Z-Score: bankruptcy-risk caution
items.impact: Flags companies at risk of financial distress, as a red flag or caution like short selling.
items.notes: Done 2026-10-10: a caution in the action's reason for the distress zone (below 1.81), never a new action, so no rules version. Banks, insurers and property trusts excluded. Shown on the Financial health card with a three-band scale.

items.title: Multiple-testing correction for track record verdicts
items.impact: Sift tests many actions over four periods, so some will pass by chance; correcting keeps the verdicts credible.
items.notes: Done 2026-10-10: Benjamini-Hochberg across every action and period (rules.adjust()), luck odds from the adjusted p-value, bars widened to the matching level (Benjamini and Yekutieli, 2005). Listed under Fixed by design.

items.title: Crash test: historical stress scenarios
items.impact: Replays 2008, the 2020 COVID fall and the 1987 crash against current holdings, in plain words.
items.notes: Part of the crash test simulator (IMP-067). Where: Portfolios, Crash test page, and a button on each portfolio. Effort: medium. Needs index history for each scenario and each holding's beta (already worked out nightly). Built in React and TypeScript (ADR-018). Full references to be checked when built, as for the statistics.

items.title: Crash test: Expected Shortfall
items.impact: Shows the average loss in the worst 1 year in 20, clearer than Value at Risk and the standard banks moved to.
items.notes: Part of IMP-067. Effort: medium. Theory: Rockafellar and Uryasev (2000). Shown as dollars for the portfolio, with a twisty for the method. Built in React and TypeScript (ADR-018). Full references to be checked when built, as for the statistics.

items.title: Crash test: fat tails and volatility clustering
items.impact: Crashes are more frequent and clustered than the simple random walk allows; this makes the crash test realistic.
items.notes: Part of IMP-067; the upgrade ADR-017 anticipates. Effort: medium. Theory: Engle (1982), Bollerslev (1986) for GARCH; Student's t for fat tails. Keep the company-page ranges simple unless users misread them.

items.title: Crash test: correlations rise in crises
items.impact: Diversification works less well in a crash; without this the crash test understates losses.
items.notes: Part of IMP-067. Effort: medium. Theory: Longin and Solnik (2001). Use stressed correlations in the scenarios rather than calm-period ones.

items.title: Fama-French attribution of the track record
items.impact: Tests whether BUY calls beat the average because of Sift's judgement or because they lean to small or cheap shares: the key credibility test.
items.notes: Where: Track record, a new card. Effort: medium to high (Australian size and value factors built from the screened universe). Start once there are about 12 months of results. Theory: Fama and French (1993, 2015). Built in React and TypeScript (ADR-018). Full references to be checked when built, as for the statistics.

items.title: Diversification check for portfolios
items.impact: Plain checks such as "your top 3 holdings are 62% of your money" and "4 of your 8 shares move together".
items.notes: Where: portfolio page, a new card. Effort: medium. Theory: Markowitz (1952); concentration measured simply. No advice on what to buy: show the facts and a help link. Built in React and TypeScript (ADR-018). Full references to be checked when built, as for the statistics.

items.title: Value and momentum evidence for the Momentum spoke
items.impact: Checks how much weight the score wheel's Momentum spoke deserves alongside cheapness.
items.notes: Where: track record analysis first, then the score wheel if justified (a rules version). Effort: medium. Theory: Jegadeesh and Titman (1993); Asness, Moskowitz and Pedersen (2013).

items.title: Disposition effect: a gentle portfolio insight
items.impact: Investors tend to sell winners too early and hold losers too long; Sift could show the pattern from a person's own sales.
items.notes: Where: portfolio page. Effort: medium. Needs careful, non-judgemental wording and no advice. Theory: Shefrin and Statman (1985); Odean (1998). Built in React and TypeScript (ADR-018). Full references to be checked when built, as for the statistics.

items.title: Beneish M-Score: possible earnings manipulation
items.impact: Flags accounts that look manipulated.
items.notes: Effort: medium to high: needs receivables, depreciation and other accounts detail Sift doesn't store yet. Theory: Beneish (1999).

items.title: Magic Formula comparison screen
items.impact: A simple, widely known value ranking (return on capital and earnings yield) to compare with Sift's results.
items.notes: Where: a screener view, not a replacement for Sift's rules. Effort: low to medium. Theory: Greenblatt (2005). Built in React and TypeScript (ADR-018). Full references to be checked when built, as for the statistics.

items.title: Kelly criterion position sizing
items.impact: Would tell people how much to put in.
items.notes: Won't do (owner's roadmap review, 2026-10-10): reads as personal advice and can encourage oversized positions.

items.title: Technical chart patterns
items.impact: Pattern signals on price charts.
items.notes: Won't do (2026-10-10): weak evidence, and they conflict with Sift's long-term value approach.

items.title: Machine learning to predict prices
items.impact: A model forecasting prices.
items.notes: Won't do (2026-10-10): hard to explain, easily overfitted, and against Sift's show-the-reasons design (ADR-017).

items.title: Rebuild the remaining pages in React and TypeScript
items.impact: One modern, typed front end instead of a 4,900-line plain JavaScript file: safer changes, richer screens (crash test, diversification), easier hand-over and a path to a phone app.
items.notes: Owner's request 2026-10-10. Like-for-like, in phases, each pushed with the app working: shared pieces (charts, tooltips, tables, table filter, dashboard layout), then pages (dashboard, screener, company, ETFs and LICs, watchlists, portfolios, track record, coattail, search, help, admin, profile and preferences, print), then the shell and router; then retire app.js, tablefilter.js and dashlayout.js. Progress: phase 1 done 2026-10-10 (foundation, Help, Track record); phase 2 done 2026-10-10 (company page).

items.title: F-Score and distress columns in the screener
items.impact: Lets people filter cheap shares by financial health without opening each company.
items.notes: The screener rows already carry f_score, f_level, z_score and z_zone; add optional columns and a ! beside the action for distress, when the screener page moves to React (IMP-084).

items.title: Richer company price chart: event dots, linked crosshair, longer periods
items.impact: Explains price moves in context (results, director trades, substantial holders) and lets long-term investors see a full cycle, without adding trading tools.
items.notes: Owner agreed 2026-10-10, to start after the React migration (IMP-084). Scope: (1) clickable event dots for results dates, director trades and substantial holder notices, with an inline summary; (2) one crosshair across the price, volume and margin of safety charts; (3) 1Y, 3Y and 5Y period buttons, with the company payload sending up to 5 years of prices; (4) an Overlays toggle for the existing 200-day average and volume, off by default. Built in Sift's own React and SVG charts (ADR-018), Sift's colours, keyboard and screen-reader support. Not doing: RSI or other technical indicators (chart patterns are Won't do), intraday prices (no live feed), news (no source), new chart, icon or animation libraries.
